newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India seen making large crude award in Oct tender.
newsitem.headline: India seen making large crude award in Oct tender.

text.p: India is expected to make a large award of crude oil in its October tender to make up for the small award it made earlier this week on diesel imports, traders said Friday.
India took just 120,000 tonnes of diesel in the October tender.
Traders attributed that to India trying to limit further congestion at its ports, where ships are backed up waiting to berth.
They said that would mean India would try to refine more products and so make a large award in its October tender.
The Indian Oil Corp (IOC) tendered last week to buy one million barrels of October crude. The tender closed on Thursday and was expected to be awarded later on Friday.
In September, IOC took three very large crude carriers (VLCCs) of Nigerian Qua Iboe and five cargoes of Dubai.
One to three cargoes of Dubai crude have been offered into India's crude buying tender for October, traders said on Friday.
They said two majors and a trader had offered Dubai. One of the majors offered at first half October quotes plus 61 cents.
A a VLCC of Bonny Light had been offered by a major and two VLCC's of Qua Iboe had also been offered, they said.
Two or three cargoes of Egypt's Suez Blend have also been offered into the tender, they said.
Traders said crude should not be affected by port congestion as it is normally discharged at offshore moorings.
